newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower after rangebound day.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower after rangebound day.

text.p: French stocks closed lower on Wednesday, knocked back into negative territory after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said he could not rule out a pre-emptive interest rate increase to head off inflation.
After starting in the red, the French market had managed to eke out a 0.35 percent gain early in the day but dropped down after Greenspan's remarks to Congress.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 5.55 points or 0.21 percent at 2,602.17 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down four points at 2,603 from Tuesday's close.
Elf rose 0.92 percent to 547 francs after reporting a 41 percent rise in 1996 net income, in line with expectations, and an increased dividend.
"There was certainly a marked improvement in results from the production and exploration side," Salomon Brothers analyst Gordon Gray told Reuters Financial Television.

Carrefour closed 2.16 percent down at 3,481. It reported lower 1996 net attributable at 3.123 billion francs, against 3.536 billion and said it wanted to increase its stake in GMB which controls the Cora store chain.

Legrand, up 0.43 percent at 976 francs, pleased the market with its result even though the figure was stable at 927 million francs. Dupont-Denant changed its recommendation to "outperform" from "market performer".
Club Med was down 5.21 percent at 427.50 francs after two days of big rises. Paribas Capital Markets changed its rating to "sell" after it had been "neutral" and previously "buy" this week.
Valeo, which reported its results on Tuesday, closed 0.97 percent higher at 384.10 francs. A number of brokerages increased their forecasts.
